correctness.rationale: Direct modalization of the source’s retained linear term \(-\chi v_*\Delta\widetilde u(t-\tau)\) gives \(+\chi v_*\mu_k\widetilde u_k(t-\tau)\). The two-by-two modal determinant therefore has delayed coefficient \(-a_{12}\chi v_*\mu_k>0\). This agrees with the source’s own zero-delay determinant Eq. (4.9) and with Song–Peng–Zhang (2021). Substitution of \(i\omega\) gives positive sine under \(P_k>0\), and elementary phase algebra shows the printed branch differs by exactly \(\pi/\omega_k\). The frequency polynomial is explicitly left unchanged because it depends on the squared coefficient.

evidence: Song–Peng–Zhang (2021), Eqs. (2.1)–(2.6), uses the same negative lower-left memory matrix and obtains the delayed determinant contribution with sign \(-d_{21}v_*a_{12}\mu_k e^{-\lambda\tau}\).

value.rationale: The corrected sign is not a cosmetic normalization: it moves every analytical Hopf-delay branch by half a temporal period while leaving the candidate frequencies unchanged. Those delay locations define the source’s minimum stability threshold and are the anchor for its Hopf analysis. Identifying the exact phase correction cleanly separates a valid zero-delay stabilization calculation from a mis-phased delayed calculation and gives a precise target for re-evaluating the stability map.
